text:
alex_dev: kicking off a canary of NF4/FP4 kernels to the dedicated-gpu pool. immediate telemetry looks... bad. ~20% throughput drop on top of 1.2x token cost, and memory high-water spikes during long chats. dumping perf/profile + logs below

canary-bot: Canary summary for run 2026-03-15T10:21Z -> throughput: -18% vs baseline, p50 latency: +40ms, p95: +120ms, mem high-water: 12GB -> 18GB on g4dn.xlarge, affected model: redwood/open-nf4-3b-fp4. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/canary/20260315/abc123 :warning:

maya_perf: :eyes: can you paste kernel selection logs? looks like fallback to slower kernels sometimes. also want KV cache hitrate and eviction stats.

alex_dev: kernel selection snippet from serving logs:
```
[2026-03-15T10:22:01Z] model=open-nf4-3b selected kernel=nf4_kernel_v1
[2026-03-15T10:22:01Z] model=open-nf4-3b fallback=fp4_int8_fallback reason=unsupported_dot
[2026-03-15T10:22:01Z] selected kernel=fp4_int8_fallback runtime_ms=9.4
[2026-03-15T10:22:01Z] selected kernel=nf4_kernel_v1 runtime_ms=5.6
```
cache stats (from metrics query): `kv_cache_hits: 3921, kv_cache_misses: 17432, evictions: 1287, current_entries: 120k` -> eviction_rate spiking during canary.

priya_ml: did the calibration use per-layer scales or global? FP4/NF4 behavior is sensitive to calibration schedule. if we used global symmetric scales we can see worse accuracy and possibly different kernel paths chosen. which calib job did you use?

alex_dev: used `calib-job: nf4-fp4-shared-scale-v2` (default on canary). priya_ml: that might explain the fallback. I can re-run per-layer calib but need test harness guidance.

jonathan_infra: also check batching distribution. telemetry shows an increase in small-batch fraction -> more kernel switches and worse amortization. I've attached batching histogram: small_batches (1-4 tokens): 64% during canary, baseline 42%.

maya_perf: that batching histogram + cache evictions = thrash. small batches increase KV writes and evictions if our cache policy is LRU and working set changes due to quantization changing KV sizes. canary config? any change to scheduler or batcher heuristics?

alex_dev: canary config diff: `kernel_priority: [nf4_kernel_v2, nf4_kernel_v1, fp4_int8_fallback]`, `batcher.max_latency_ms: 15 -> 10 (tightened)`, `kv_cache.max_entries: 200k -> 120k (reduced)` (we tried to save memory).
this combination probably caused aggressive trimming of cache + more small batches -> fallbacks and OOM spikes.

maya_perf: ok - the reduced kv_cache cap is suspicious. lowering entries saves memory per-host but increases miss rate and forces loads which spike memory transiently and increase latencies. two immediate mitigations:
- revert kv_cache cap to baseline 200k
- relax batcher.max_latency back to 15ms so small-batches coalesce

alex_dev: running rollback of kv_cache cap now, will patch batcher config in 5m. rolling back FP4 kernel selection to prefer nf4_kernel_v2-only for canary too.

priya_ml: I'll run a calibration sweep with per-layer symmetric scales + per-tensor asymmetric as a comparison. also will produce microbench for kernels across sequence lengths [8,32,128,512] and batch sizes [1,2,4,8]. expected outcome: nf4_kernel_v2 should be fastest at medium seq len and tolerate quantization; fp4_int8 fallback only when ops unsupported.

alex_dev: quick microbench we ran locally:
```
model: open-nf4-3b
seq_len=128 batch=4 -> nf4_kernel_v2: 55 tokens/s, fp4_int8_fallback: 34 tokens/s
seq_len=32 batch=1 -> nf4_kernel_v2: 18 tokens/s, fp4_int8_fallback: 16 tokens/s
seq_len=512 batch=8 -> nf4_kernel_v2: 42 tokens/s, fp4_int8_fallback: 24 tokens/s
```
these match the canary direction when fallbacks increase.

jonathan_infra: are kernel selection decisions logged with reasons? we need to add more telemetry: `kernel_reason` tag per request (e.g., shape_mismatch, unsupported_dot, runtime_oom, preferred). that'll let us filter where fallback triggers.

maya_perf: agreed. also add `kv_cache_eviction_reason` (size_limit vs ttl) so we know if we trimmed proactively.

sre_oncall: FYI this caused two customer incidents (IDs INC-2026-091 and INC-2026-092). please triage and update the incident tickets with rollback notes. if rollback reduces customer impact, escalate to postmortem.

alex_dev: rolling back FP4 selection and kv_cache cap now. patching batcher.max_latency to 15ms in canary config. will re-run canary after priya's calib sweep and jonathan's added telemetry.

priya_ml: I'll share calibration artifacts and perf deltas by EOD. also will add a suggested quant scheme matrix for nf4 vs fp4 (per-layer vs global) so we have deterministic fallback triggers.

alex_dev: thanks team. temporary mitigation timeline: rollback in 10m, added telemetry in 2h, full calib + microbench and new canary tomorrow morning. tagging @oncall for visibility. :thumbsup: 

canary-bot: Canary rollback executed for run 20260315/abc123 by alex_dev at 2026-03-15T10:35Z. New canary pending.

alex_dev: ack, following up with logs and final perf diff once new canary runs.
